slides.title: How are particles arranged in each state?
bullets: In a SOLID, particles are packed tightly together in a fixed arrangement — they vibrate but do not move past each other.
In a LIQUID, particles are close together but can slide past each other — the material flows and takes the shape of its container.
In a GAS, particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions — they fill any space available.

sections.text: Sort each material into solid, liquid or gas. Write one reason for each, using the particle model below to help you.
Can you find one material that is difficult to classify? Why?

sections.words: solid  •  liquid  •  gas  •  particles  •  closely packed  •  slide past  •  spread out  •  fixed shape  •  flows

answers: Particles packed tightly in a fixed arrangement, so ice keeps its shape.
Particles are close but can slide past each other, so water flows and takes the shape of its container.
Particles move quickly and are spread far apart, so steam fills the space available.
Particles are fixed in place, so wood keeps its shape and does not flow.
Each grain is a solid with its own fixed shape, but lots of grains together can pour like a liquid.
Particles slide past each other, so milk flows and takes the shape of its container.
The air particles inside move quickly and spread out to fill the balloon.
Honey flows very slowly, but it is still a liquid because it takes the shape of its container.

sections.text: Sand and honey are the best examples.
Sand: a single grain is a solid with its own fixed shape, but a big pile of grains can be poured and takes the shape of its container - a bit like a liquid.
Honey: it is a liquid because it takes the shape of its container, but it flows so slowly it can look almost solid.
